body:
## Why

An attempt that dies **before** it opens its PR has no automatic path back to its own work, even though
the work is sitting on a branch hkb named itself.

Hit on #304, 2026-09-03. Attempt 1 ran about an hour, made three good commits on `worktree-kb-304-1`,
and was reclaimed when its Claude session daemon died (`control.sock` ENOENT) — before opening a PR. The
tick was right to reclaim it. But hkb's continuation keys on an **open PR**: `continues_pr` is set when
the dispatcher finds one for the card, and the worker brief then says "continue it". With no PR there was
nothing to continue, so attempt 2 was dispatched to start from `main` and would have redone the hour.

What actually saved it was manual: the operator pushed the branch, committed the 13 uncommitted files as a
labelled recovery commit, and wrote a note on the card telling the next attempt where to look. That worked
— attempt 3 continued from it and reported the recovered WIP was accurate — but none of it is a mechanism.

The information needed was all present and machine-readable the whole time: the branch is
`worktree-kb-<n>-<k>` (or `kb-<n>-<k>`), hkb generates that name itself, and `taskBranchRe` already exists
to match it.

## What

1. When the dispatcher builds a worker brief for attempt `k+1` and finds **no open PR**, look for a branch
   matching this card's naming convention that has commits the default branch does not. If there is one,
   say so in the brief the way `continues_pr` does: which branch, how many commits ahead, and that the
   attempt should continue rather than restart.
2. Prefer the newest such branch when several attempts left one; name them all when it is ambiguous rather
   than guessing.
3. A branch that exists only locally is worth naming too — but the brief must say it is unpushed, because
   a fresh worktree cannot see it. (Deciding whether hkb should *push* an abandoned attempt's branch is
   part of this card: it makes the work durable, and it also puts commits on the remote that no PR
   explains. Argue it either way on the card.)
4. `hkb show <n>` and `hkb log <n>` mention an orphaned branch, since the operator is the one who
   currently has to notice.

## Done when

- [ ] An attempt killed after committing but before opening a PR leaves a branch that the next attempt's
      brief names, with its commit count.
- [ ] The brief distinguishes "continue this PR" from "continue this branch, no PR yet".
- [ ] Tests for: no branch, one branch, several branches, and a branch already merged into the default
      branch (which must NOT be offered).
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` green.

## Contract

Do not change what happens when a PR *does* exist — that path works. Do not force-push or rewrite any
branch. Keep `src/gh.js`/`src/forge.js` as the only places that reach the forge.
title: An attempt that dies before opening its PR loses its commits: continuation keys on the PR, not the branch
